3.text: the Sea Being, though they are not identified with Kereˊtkun.

4.text: Among the symbols of game killed, there are to be found, besides the

5.text: animals already mentioned, parts of the nose of the walrus, the skulls of various

6.text: sea-birds (for example, of murres and eider-ducks), as well as their wooden

7.text: images. Seals and other sea-animals are represented by images of wood.

8.text: The charm represented in Fig. 255 has two “guardians” (a, b), one of

9.text: which is armed with a knife, a small dog (c), a small image of the fire-drill

10.text: board (d), and two pieces of wood without any definite signification.

11.text: The charm shown in Fig. 256 contains a part of the upper lip of a

12.text: walrus (a), a rough leathern image of a “guardian” (b), a wooden image of

13.text: a sea-spirit with human head and the tail of a fish (c), a wooden bird (d), a

14.text: round piece of wood representing a divining-tool (e), an image of the head

15.text: of a fire-drill board charred in the fire to make the likeness more apparent (f),

16.text: a piece of bone forming a divining-tool (g), a leathern image of a “guardian” (h),

17.text: and three claws of a seal (i, j, k).

18.text: In Fig. 257, a and b represent an image of a sea-spirit and its dog, both

19.text: parts of charm-strings; c shows a double-headed image which belonged to a charm-

20.text: string of an inhabitant of Mariinsky Post, a sort of Chukchee blacksmith with

21.text: very little skill. He told me that one of the heads represented himself, and

22.text: the other his “assistant” in the blacksmith’s craft. This “assistant,” among other

23.text: things, attended very carefully to securing prompt payment for the blacksmith’s

24.text: work. In the case of slow payments, he punished both the workman and the

25.text: customer. He was apparently jealous because his activity as “assistant” was

26.text: slightingly treated: therefore he was angry with both parties. In one case,

27.text: when the blacksmith failed to collect the fee for mending a kettle, the

28.text: “assistant” became so angry, that while the blacksmith was at work he jumped

29.text: into his left eye in the form of a red spark. As a result, the eye was

30.text: seriously hurt, and the dilatory customer was soon afterward stricken with palsy.
